title: Lease-based node winback protocol for throughput contracts
creator: Mira Santos
description:
Problem: During planned node lifecycle events (maintenance, upgrades, preemptions) Dedicated fleets occasionally drop short-lived capacity below per-tenant throughput contracts, causing transient latency spikes and tail SLO violations. Current drain workflows rely on immediate eviction or long manual drain windows; both either cause customer-visible throughput loss or waste capacity.

Proposal: Implement a lease-based node winback protocol layered on top of routing and autoscaler logic. Nodes acquire short-duration throughput leases that represent their available contribution to per-tenant throughput contracts. When a node needs to enter maintenance, it posts an early withdraw intent and enters a 'drain runway' state: existing leases are gradually released back to the routing pool while the system orchestrates prewarming of replacement hosts, KV-cache snapshot warmup, and traffic handoff according to contract priorities. The protocol should allow: (1) graceful, time-bounded handshake between node and fleet controller; (2) soft-reservations for critical customers (reserved lanes) during maintenance; (3) autoscaler hedging to provision buffer capacity ahead of lease expiry; (4) clear telemetry for lease churn and prewarm success rates.

Goals:
- Maintain per-tenant throughput contracts (units/sec) during routine maintenance with >=99.95% adherence for P0/P1 customers.
- Reduce customer-observed latency p99 spikes during rolling upgrades by 60% vs current baseline.
- Avoid over-provisioning: autoscaler hedges limited to 12% of committed capacity for scheduled waves.

Constraints & considerations:
- Protocol must be origin-agnostic: work for Hosted/Dedicated/Private with local control plane variants.
- KVS/Transformer cache warm-up cost tradeoffs: full snapshot vs incremental preheat.
- Must integrate with existing routing fallback that can route to compatible model variants when capacity tight.
- Security: lease tokens are short-lived cryptographic tokens; revocation must be auditable and logged to central audit log.

Success metrics (initial):
- Throughput contract adherence (per-tenant) >=99.95% during maintenance windows.
- p99 latency delta <= +10ms for critical routes.
- Prewarm hit rate >= 85% within lease handoff window.
- Autoscaler hedge cost under budget (<1.2x baseline monthly committed spend for fleets during rollout).
acceptance_criteria: Protocol defined and documented: handshake, states (active, runway, handoff, retired), token semantics and TTL
Routing accepts lease tokens and enforces lane reservations at request-time
Autoscaler integrates with lease signals and provisions hedges within configured bounds
KV prewarm API implemented and tested in canary (region us-west-2) with >=85% prewarm success
Runbook and playbook for lease-revocation incidents in Console + PagerDuty integration
E2E chaos experiment verifies no more than P0 customers experience throughput degradation >5% during scheduled maintenance
tasks: Design proto: state machine & message formats (mira/2025-01-12)
Lease token implementation in node-agent (eng-runner): create/renew/revoke endpoints (jonah)
Routing changes: accept lease headers and gate by lane reservations (routing-team)
Autoscaler: hedging policy hook and budget limiter (autoscale-team)
KV prewarm: snapshot export/import and incremental warm APIs (cache-team)
E2E tests: synthetic workload + canary rollout (qa)
Runbook: incident steps, rollback criteria, mitigation links
risks: Lease token abuse if not properly authenticated — mitigated by short TTL and KMS-signed tokens
Autoscaler could over-hedge leading to cost overruns — implement hard budget cap per fleet
KV prewarm may not reach parity for cold models; fall back to routing to compatible variants
Cross-region handoff latencies may increase; restrict initial rollout to single-region fleets

implementation_notes: Lease token format: base64(KMS-signed {node_id, ttl, lanes, revision})
State transitions: active -> runway(with runway_ttl) -> handoff -> retired; node must advertise prewarm manifest on entering runway
Routing uses soft-priority queue where reserved lanes are honored before best-effort traffic; routers decrement lease counters on token consumption
Autoscaler exposes hedging API: create_buffer(fleet_id, capacity_units, max_cost_ratio, signal_expiry)
Audit events: lease.create, lease.renew, lease.revoke emitted to central event store with request_id
